file_id: 498A-304B Of TheIndianPenalCodevs In Re : Anadi Pandey @ Dip on 8 June, 2023

sentences.text:
vs In Re : Anadi Pandey @
Dip on 8 June, 2023 08.06.2023 sdas allowed CRM(DB) No. 2161 of 2023 In Re:- An application for bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with Ranaghat Police Station Case No. 65 of 2023 dated 09.02.2023 under Sections 498A/304B of the Indian Penal Code.
And In Re : Anadi Pandey @ Dip ...... petitioner Mr. Prabir Majumder Mr. S. Majumder .....for the petitioner Mr. P. K. Datta, learned APP Mr. Santanu Deb Roy ..... for the State Liberty is granted to correct the cause title.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits allegation of demand of dowry is not supported by neighbours.
It is also submitted that on the fateful day there was altercation between the couple.
Due to emotional outburst housewife suddenly took her life.
Learned Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail and submits victim housewife died within one and half years of marriage.
We have considered the materials on record.
Allegation of torture over demand of dowry is not supported by neighbours.
There is no possibility of abscondence.
Under such circumstances, we are inclined to grant bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, we direct that the petitioner shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranaghat, Nadia, subject to the condition that petitioner shall appear before the trial court on every date of hearing until further orders and shall not intimidate the witnesses and/or tamper with evidence in any manner whatsoever.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranaghat, Nadia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the event the petitioner fails to appear before the trial court without justifiable cause, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel his bail in accordance with law without further reference to this Court.
The application for bail is, accordingly, allowed.

(Joymalya Bagchi, J.)
